Rand-OFDM, which leverages the flexibility of randomization in orthogonal frequency
division multiplexing systems. By applying randomization to the subcarrier domain,
Rand-OFDM ensures that only the intended receiver can accurately interpret the
original signal characteristics, such as its power distribution and bit sequence.
This secure method exploits the inherent complexity of randomization, making it
difficult for unauthorized parties to obtain valuable information. We examine the
security of Rand-OFDM through a comprehensive analysis of its vulnerability to
eavesdroppers, which involves assessing the receiver's ability to deduce the
original signal statistics. Our analysis reveals that Rand-OFDM offers a high level
of security, with only a negligible increase in required transmit power. Furthermore,
Rand-OFDM's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations that show its ability to
protect sensitive information, such as bit sequences, from eavesdroppers. This
approach can be seamlessly integrated into existing OFDM systems, making it a
practical solution for secure communication. Our findings also highlight the
importance of considering the security implications of randomization in
communication systems. Finally, Rand-OFDM's potential to enhance the security of
Internet of Things (IoT) devices is explored, with potential applications in
protecting IoT networks from cyber threats. This research contributes to the
development of secure IoT networks, with Rand-OFDM serving as a valuable tool.

To address this issue, we propose the LAtent bounDary-guided aDvErsarial training (LADDER) framework, which leverages latent boundary information to strike a balance between robustness and generalizability. By incorporating a novel boundary loss function, LADDER encourages models to learn boundaries that are both robust and accurate. Experimental results demonstrate that LADDER outperforms existing adversarial training methods in terms of both robustness and generalizability. Furthermore, our framework can be seamlessly integrated with existing adversarial training techniques to yield improved results. This research focuses on optimizing appointment scheduling for customers with uncertain travel and service times. Moreover, we identify a critical parameter threshold beyond which the system transitions from a stable state to a more complex synchronized state. In the realm of High Energy Physics, data compression is a crucial aspect that significantly influences not only the initial data creation process, but also subsequent analysis stages. This paper delves into the compression of simulation data generated by Pythia 8, focusing on the impact of compression on data retrieval during analysis. To achieve this, we employ a lossless compression technique, and subsequently, decompress the data on a per-event basis. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of compression on the underlying physics, and provide recommendations for optimal compression usage. Our findings indicate that judicious compression can result in considerable time savings during analysis, with a corresponding increase in data access time of up to 10% for a single event. Moreover, we discovered that the data compression process does not compromise the physics integrity. Notably, we observed that the data compression rate is contingent upon the event size, with smaller events yielding higher compression ratios. Based on our research, we propose that data compression can be effectively utilized in various simulation scenarios, and recommend its implementation in future Pythia 8 versions. This study serves as a valuable reference for other simulation tools, and we encourage the adoption of our methods in similar contexts. The accompanying code is publicly accessible on the GitHub platform at https://github.com/roberto-fernandez/Pythia8Compression. Deep learning models have been successfully applied in various tasks, but their effectiveness is often hindered by the need for a large number of labeled training samples. To address this limitation, active learning methods have been developed to efficiently select the most informative samples for annotation. To strike a balance between these two approaches, we propose a novel active learning method that utilizes a two-stage sampling strategy. Initially, we identify the most representative samples within each class, and then select the most similar samples to these class representatives. This approach ensures that the model learns from a diverse set of samples while maintaining a strong understanding of each class. To further enhance the model's performance, we incorporate a self-supervised learning stage, where the model is trained on unlabeled data to improve its ability to generalize. Our proposed method is evaluated on three benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate its superiority over existing state-of-the-art methods. Diabetic foot ulcers pose a significant risk to individuals with diabetes, necessitating precise and timely monitoring to prevent potential complications. However, the process of tracking these ulcers can be time-consuming and prone to errors due to the subjective nature of human interpretation. To address this challenge, we propose utilizing image-to-image translation techniques to create a more efficient and effective monitoring system. By leveraging a deep learning model that can translate a patient's initial foot ulcer image into a simulated image representing the wound after a specified period, healthcare professionals can more accurately assess the progression of the ulcer. To evaluate the performance of our model, we conducted a study involving 12 participants, who were tasked with identifying changes in simulated images generated from real foot ulcers. The results indicate that our model can significantly enhance the accuracy of ulcer monitoring, with a 90% increase in correct identifications over traditional methods. Furthermore, the model's ability to generalize to unseen data sets was also demonstrated, with a high success rate of 85% in translating images from a different data set. Overall, the findings suggest that our image-to-image translation model can be a valuable tool for improving the monitoring of diabetic foot ulcers. To address this issue, we introduce a novel attention mechanism that enables real-time semantic segmentation models to achieve state-of-the-art performance. This mechanism, called Cross-Resolution Attention, leverages the unique characteristics of different spatial resolutions to enhance the accuracy of segmentation. By combining features from multiple resolutions, Cross-Resolution Attention effectively captures the intricate details of the input image. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by integrating it into the highly efficient Bi-Linear model, resulting in a new state-of-the-art real-time semantic segmentation model that achieves a remarkable 70.1 mIoU on the Cityscapes validation set while operating at 100.8 FPS. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in various ranking tasks, outperforming existing methods. In continuous control problems, the standard approach of using an exploration strategy to gather data from all possible states is often inefficient. This is because it can lead to a significant amount of time being spent exploring states that are unlikely to be encountered during actual task execution. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that involves training a policy to operate within a limited range of states that are easily accessible and can be explored thoroughly. By doing so, we can minimize the prediction error associated with these states and, as a result, improve the agent's performance on the target task. To achieve this, we employ a technique called state abstraction, which enables us to identify a small set of representative states that capture the essence of the task. These states are then used to train a policy that operates within a limited domain, and we demonstrate that this approach can lead to a significant reduction in exploration time while maintaining high task performance. To validate the effectiveness of our method, we conducted experiments on a range of continuous control tasks and observed a substantial reduction in exploration time, with some tasks requiring as little as 1% of the original data. This approach is particularly useful in scenarios where data collection is expensive or time-consuming, and we believe it has the potential to be applied to a broader range of reinforcement learning problems. Additionally, we propose a hierarchical PGI framework that leverages the benefits of both hierarchical and non-hierarchical methods. Our approach involves a two-stage process, where the first stage utilizes a generative adversarial network to produce synthetic data, and the second stage evaluates the quality of the generated data. By distributing the data and the necessary resources across a blockchain network, our decentralized solution enables the creation of synthetic data without compromising data privacy. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we conducted a case study using the Swedish National Patient Registry and found that our decentralized solution can produce high-quality synthetic data. Furthermore, the use of our decentralized solution can significantly reduce the time and cost required to generate synthetic data. This paper delves into the representation theory of weighted quiver mutation, 
which is a generalization of cluster mutation found in cluster algebras. 
We derive a formula for the group generated by weighted quiver mutation, 
and establish a connection between this formula and the quantum cluster 
algebra. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of triangular bases, 
which is a broader framework encompassing quantum cluster algebras and their generalizations. 
We prove that triangular bases can be decomposed into irreducible components 
and provide a combinatorial description of these components. 
We also establish a connection between the quantum cluster algebra and the triangular basis. 
Finally, we introduce the notion of cluster-tilted quivers and show that they yield 
a set of triangular bases, which is a generalization of the cluster tilting property. 
This work is motivated by the desire to extend the results of cluster algebras 
to the quantum cluster algebra context. 
We also explore the potential applications of weighted quiver mutation in 
the study of quantum cluster algebras.

Flow Lenia is a variant of the cellular automata-based game 'Lenia,' which
allows for the integration of dynamic parameters within its environment. This
results in the emergence of diverse, dynamic phenomena, including oscillations,
within a continuous space. In contrast to traditional cellular automata, which
operate on discrete time and space, Flow Lenia utilizes floating-point numbers to
define its underlying grid. This paper presents a new cellular automata-based
model, which we call 'Flow Lenia,' and demonstrates its ability to replicate
the behavior of the original Flow Lenia. Furthermore, we investigate the
relationship between the parameters of the Flow Lenia model and its resulting
dynamics. Our findings suggest that the Flow Lenia model can generate a wide
range of dynamic behaviors, including oscillations, which are influenced by the
parameters of the underlying cellular automata. Additionally, we examine the
computational complexity of the Flow Lenia model and its potential applications
in the field of artificial life. Finally, we discuss the potential for future
research in the area of artificial life, which could involve the development of
new cellular automata-based models that incorporate dynamic parameters. This
research has the potential to lead to the creation of novel artificial life
forms, which could exhibit complex behaviors and interactions. Ultimately, we
believe that the study of Flow Lenia and other cellular automata-based models
will contribute significantly to the advancement of the field of artificial life.

The conventional approach to video classification, which involves training a model on a fixed set of videos, is inefficient due to its slow training speed. To address this issue, we propose a new paradigm that utilizes a dynamic set of videos for training, allowing the model to be updated at a faster rate. By leveraging a large video dataset and a pre-trained model, we can create a continuously evolving set of videos for training, which we refer to as the "active set." This approach enables us to train the model on the active set, using a ranking-based method to select the most relevant videos for training. To further enhance the training process, we introduce a novel loss function that takes into account the uncertainty of the model's predictions. By using this loss function, we can identify videos that are difficult to classify and prioritize them for training, leading to improved performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves a significant 2.5 times speedup in training time while maintaining comparable or even better performance compared to the conventional approach. Additionally, our method is shown to be more efficient than other state-of-the-art active learning methods, with a speedup of 1.5 to 2 times. We establish a Galois covering on a tropical curve by assigning a finite
extension of the valuation field, where the Galois group acts on the curve's
tropical structure in a piecewise linear manner. This construction enables us to
derive a Galois correspondence for tropical curves, analogous to the classical
Galois correspondence for algebraic curves. Furthermore, we prove that
tropical functions satisfy a weak version of the Fundamental Theorem of Galois
Theory for finite extensions of the valuation field. Specifically, we show that
for any finite extension, there exists a tropical function that matches the
ramification behavior of the original extension. This result is applied to
investigate the properties of tropical curves, including their abelian varieties
and the behavior of finite morphisms. Additionally, we demonstrate that the
cardinality of the automorphism group of a tropical curve is determined by its
genus and degree. Finally, we provide a Galois correspondence for finite
morphisms of tropical curves, analogous to the classical Galois correspondence
for algebraic curves. This research is motivated by the work of the second
author, who previously developed a Galois correspondence for algebraic curves.

Our study demonstrates the potential of reinforcement learning to develop efficient control strategies for quantum cooling, with C-DQN emerging as a promising approach. gaining a deep understanding of the relationship between video and text. To

unlabeled video-text data to learn a more nuanced understanding of the
relationship between video and text. VICTOR achieves this by learning a joint
representation of video and text that can be used to generate coherent and
meaningful text descriptions of videos. This approach is more challenging than
previous methods, as it requires the model to generate text that accurately
